memory_graph/gdlmem.py record <id> (the supersedes/superseded_by/refutes fields quoted above)
falsifier: Re-run the index at any later commit: this law dies if the family's supersession/refutation edge count rises to cover the three unmarked corrections named above, or if it can be shown that `gdlmem.py laws`/`brief` already de-ranks a law whose text is contradicted by a newer record with no edge (it does not -- both correcting and corrected laws appear in `laws --query addr16` with no status distinction between them, which is the observation this law rests on). It is also falsified if some OTHER field carries the correction machine-readably for these three pairs; the index script reads `supersedes`, `superseded_by` and `refutes` on every record and finds nothing else pointing at them.
subject: tool:gdl-memory-graph
value: A LAW THAT CORRECTS ANOTHER LAW MUST CARRY `supersedes` OR `refutes`, BECAUSE PUBLISHING THE CORRECTION AS A NEW LAW LEAVES THE CORRECTED CLAUSE LIVE, UNMARKED, AND USUALLY OLDER-AND-THEREFORE-FIRST IN A KEYWORD SEARCH. MEASURED at 84f85a96a over the sixteen live laws of the addr16/live-zero family (every record file under memory_graph/records/ read and indexed; 2234 records; the family enumerated by `gdlmem.py laws --query addr16` and `--query "live zero"` and then filtered to the ADDR16_LO / addrlo / live-zero / zero-remat slugs): EXACTLY ONE supersession edge exists in the entire family -- claim.law.addr16-lo-address-homed-via-r0-is-source-unreachable.20260831.v2 supersedes its own v1. Every other correction in the family, including four published the SAME DAY as the record they correct, is a standalone law with `supersedes: None`, `superseded_by: None` and `refutes: None`. The only two inbound `refutes` edges in the family come from ATTEMPT records, never from the correcting laws: attempt.loaditems-addrlo-home-copy-cap.20260901.v1 -> claim.law.addr16-lo-home-copy-census-no-source-discriminant.20260831.v1, and attempt.CR_processcritterlist-the-declaration-order-lever-is-inert-here-so-the-addr16lo-reachable-remainder-is-zero.20260904.v1 -> claim.law.AL_the-addr16lo-surplus-copy-roster-is-two-classes-split-by-destination-register-and-only-the-volatile-tenth-is-reachable.20260904.v1. THE THREE UNMARKED CORRECTIONS, each verbatim from the correcting record's own text: (1) claim.law.AL_the-addrlo-home-copy-survives-scheduling-off-so-the-prologue-shadow-is-a-symptom.20260904.v1 says of claim.law.addr16-lo-home-copy-census-no-source-discriminant.20260831.v1's FINDING 3 that 'THAT STATISTIC IS A TAUTOLOGY' and of claim.law.addrlo-home-copy-class-is-general-temp-and-shadow-coupled.20260901.v1's FINDING 3 ('ONE event, observationally inseparable') that 'The two halves ARE separable, and one build separates them' -- and carries no edge to either. (2) claim.law.CR_the-pre-frame-addr16lo-r0-versus-named-volatile-discriminator-has-a-counter-example-and-the-census-floor-is-the-reason.20260904.v1 is titled a 'BOUNDARY AND CORRECTION on claim.law.NC_pre-frame-addr16-lo-into-r0-owes-a-callee-saved-copy.20260903.v1' and states that law's discriminator 'does not hold in the direction it is stated' -- and carries no edge to it, so NC's two-group split still reads as settled. (3) claim.law.AL_addrlo-class-recensused-at-head-s-is-not-zero-and-five-more-discriminants-die.20260904.v1 states that the S=0 one-directionality 'does NOT extend to the volatile-home variant' -- narrowing the scope of two parent laws that still assert it unqualified. CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this is a law rather than a tidiness complaint: `gdlmem.py laws` ranks newest-first and prints `supersession`, and AGENTS.md instructs a lane to 'check `superseded_by` before applying an old law'. That instruction is only as good as the edges, and in this family it returns 'not superseded' for three laws whose decisive clauses have been measured false. A lane screening by keyword hits the ORIGINAL wording first, because the original owns the family's canonical slug words ('addr16-lo-home-copy-census-no-source-discriminant' matches `--query addr16` on id, slug and text, while the correcting law matches on text alone). THE RULE: if your record's own prose says another record is wrong, incomplete, tautological, or narrower than it claims, the edge is not optional -- `supersedes` when you are replacing it, `refutes` when you are disproving a mechanism it asserts. Writing the correction only in prose is the graph equivalent of leaving a stale comment in the code.
